facts.statement: The remains of Bonapartesaurus were excavated by Jaime Powell and collaborators in 1984 and formally described by Powell in 1987.
facts.quote: The remains were excavated by the Argentine paleontologist Jaime Powell and collaborators in 1984 and described by him in 1987

facts.statement: In its initial description, Powell identified the remains as a possible indeterminate lambeosaurine, comparing them to Hypacrosaurus and Barsboldia based on the large size of the neural spines.
facts.quote: where he identified the dinosaur remains as a possible "indeterminate lambeosaurine", comparing it mainly with the genera Hypacrosaurus and Barsboldia due to great size of the neural spines

facts.statement: In 2017, Cruzado-Caballero and Powell reclassified the paratype of Willinakaqe salitralensis as the new species Bonapartesaurus rionegrensis, declaring the former name invalid due to it being a chimera of different hadrosaurids.
facts.quote: In a 2017 study, Cruzado-Caballero and Powell (who died before the paper was published) reassigned the paratype of W. salitralensis to its own genus and species, Bonapartesaurus rionegrensis, converting the former into a chimera of different hadrosaurids, and hence, an invalid name

facts.statement: The holotype specimen consists of a partial skeleton containing numerous vertebrae, ribs, limb bones, and an almost complete articulated left foot.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen MPCA-Pv SM2/1-71, consists of a partial skeleton including 4 dorsal vertebrae, a complete sacrum, 8 anterior caudal vertebrae, 9 medial caudal vertebrae, 2 blocks with 5 medial caudal vertebrae each, 18 haemal arches, 3 dorsal ribs, a distal fragment of the right scapula, a distal fragment of the left humerus, a left ulna, a right ilium, a nearly complete left pubis, distal fragments of both ischia, both femurs, tibias, and fibulae, a left astragalus, a right calcaneus, an almost complete articulated left foot and two blocks with tendons

facts.statement: CT scans performed in 2021 revealed three paleopathologies on the holotype bones, including fractures and a tumor.
facts.quote: In 2021, Cruzado-Caballero and colleagues used CT scans to identify three palaeopathologies present on the bones of the Bonapartesaurus holotype

facts.statement: A tumor found in the metatarsal bone was likely a malignant bone tumor such as osteosarcoma.
facts.quote: There was a tumour in the metatarsal bone which was probably a malignant bone tumour such as osteosarcoma

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the identified pathologies caused pain and impaired function but were not the direct cause of death.
facts.quote: These pathologies likely caused pain and hampered the animal's normal functioning, but were not the direct cause of its death

facts.statement: Bonapartesaurus is classified within the tribe Kritosaurini.
Bonapartesaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, between the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages, approximately 70 million years ago in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a durante el Cretácico Superior, entre el Campaniense y el Maastrichtiense, hace aproximadamente 70 millones de años en lo que es hoy Sudamérica

facts.statement: It is debated whether the material previously attributed to Willinakaqe represents more than one taxon, with researchers concluding that the original diagnostic characteristics were invalid.
facts.quote: Later, the Spanish paleontologist Penélope Cruz-Caballero and the Argentine Rodolfo Coria reviewed the material attributed to the genus Willinakaqe in 2016, where they concluded that fossils may represent more than one taxon of hadrosaurid and that the characteristics used in the diagnosis would not be valid

facts.statement: The holotype specimen is a partial skeleton containing dorsal vertebrae, a complete sacrum, caudal vertebrae, ribs, limb bones, and a nearly complete articulated left foot.
facts.quote: El holotipo MPCA-Pv SM2/1-71, consta de un esqueleto parcial que incluye 4 vértebras dorsales, un sacro completo , 8 vértebras caudales anteriores, 9 vértebras caudales mediales, 2 bloques con 5 vértebras caudales mediales cada uno, 18 arcos hemales, 3 costillas dorsales, un fragmento distal del lámina escapular derecha, un fragmento distal del húmero izquierdo, un cúbito izquierdo, ilión derecho, un pubis izquierdo casi completa, fragmentos distales de ambos isquiones, ambos fémures, tibias, y fíbulas, un astrágalo izquierdo, un calcáneo derecho, un pie izquierdo articulado casi completo y dos bloques con tendones.

facts.statement: Fossils were found at the Salitral Moreno site in southern Argentina within the lower member of the Allen Formation, dating to the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Todo el material presente fue extraído del sitio Salitral Moreno de la provincia de Río Negro en el sur de Argentina, del miembro inferior de la Formación Allen, la cual data del Cretácico superior.

facts.statement: Argentine paleontologist Jaime Powell excavated the remains in 1984 and described the species in 1987, initially identifying it as an indeterminate Lambeosaurine.
facts.quote: Los restos fueron excavados por el paleontólogo argentino Jaime Powell y colaboradores en 1984 y descrito por el mismo en 1987, donde identificó el holotipo de Bonapartesaurus como un posible "Lambeosaurinae indeterminado", comparándolo principalmente con los géneros Hypacrosaurus y Barsboldia por las espinas neurales de gran tamaño.

facts.statement: Researchers debated the validity of the genus Willinakaqe in 2016, concluding that its fossils likely represented multiple hadrosaurid taxa rather than a single species.
facts.quote: Posteriormente la paleontóloga española Penélope Cruzado-Caballero y su homólogo argentino Rodolfo Coria revisaron el material atribuido al género Willinakaqe en 2016, donde concluyeron que los fósiles pueden representar más de un taxón de hadrosáurido y que las características usadas en la diagnosis no tendrían validez.

facts.statement: In 2017, Cruzado-Caballero and Powell reclassified the main paratype of Willinakaqe as Bonapartesaurus rionegrensis, rendering Willinakaqe a invalid name due to it being a chimera of different hadrosaurids.
facts.quote: En 2017 Cruzado-Caballero y Powell reasignan el paratipo principal de W. salitralensis a su propio género y especie, Bonapartesaurus rionegrensis, convirtiendo al primero en una quimera de diferentes hadrosáuridos, y por ende, en un nombre inválido.

facts.statement: Bonapartesaurus is classified within the Hadrosauridae family, specifically following an older definition of Hadrosaurinae that includes non-crested hadrosaurids.
facts.quote: El análisis filogenético de Bonapartesaurus sigue la definición de Paul Sereno para Hadrosauridae de 1998, además de usar la clasificación antigua de Hadrosaurinae (antes del consenso de Prieto-Márquez en 2010), donde se incluyen a todos los hadrosáuridos no crestados junto con el género fragmentario Hadrosaurus dentro de la misma subfamilia.

facts.statement: The species is placed in the tribe Saurolophini, positioned as more derived than Prosaurolophus but more basal than Saurolophus species.
facts.quote: Asimismo, se le coloca dentro de la tribu Saurolophini, siendo más derivado que Prosaurolophus, pero más basal que Saurolophus spp., contrastando con la clasificación tentativa de Willinakaqe dentro de la tribu Kritosaurini.

facts.statement: A 2022 revision reclassified Bonapartesaurus into the tribe Kritosaurini as part of a new South American clade including Huallasaurus and Secernosaurus.
facts.quote: En 2022 una revisión de los hadrosáuridos de finales del Cretácico de la Patagonia reasigna a Bonapartesaurus a Kritosaurini, clasificación inicial de Willinakaqe, en un nuevo clado de hadrosáuridos sudamericanos compuesto por el nuevo taxón, Huallasaurus, Bonapartesaurus y Secernosaurus.

facts.statement: The animal lived during the Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
